2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted a suit praying for a decree of pre-emption under Mahomedan Law contending, inter-alia, that the land comprising .64 acre of land of plot No. 413 appertaining to R.S. khatian No. 52 originally belonged to Shah Monsur Ali, Shah Entazur Rahma, Shah Md. Badiuzzaman, Shah Md. Taimur, Shah Md. Babu Mia and their sisters where Shah Md. Badiuzzama became the owner of four annas share i.e. .16 acre of land. While said recorded owner Shah Md. Badiuzzaman was owning and possessing the said .16 acre of land, transferred to Mirza Abul Kashem, the defendant No. 8 by way of registered deed dated 27.05.1957 and delivered possession thereon. The defendant No. 12 for the purpose of Road and Highways acquired .42 acre of land of suit plot No. 413 and the rest .22 acre of land was owned and possessed by Shah Monsur Ali two anna share, Shah Entazur Rahman in ten anna share and Mirza Abul Kashem in four annas share, but S.A. khatian No. 74 has been wrongly prepared in the R.S. recorded owners. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that there is no cause of action, the suit is bad for defect of parties and also barred by limitation and .64 acre of land of R.S. suit khatian No. 52 originally belonged to Shah Mansur Ali, Shah Entazur Rahman, Shah Badiuzzamn Khan, Shah Md. Taimur, Asiya Khatun, Nasima Khatun, A. Razzaque, Shah Md. Babu Mia, Hashina Khatun, Halimunnessa and Surjajan Bibi, and so the statement of the plaint of the plaintiff that four anna share of the suit khatian owned and possessed by Shah Md. Badiuzzaman, Shah Md. Taimur and Shah Md. Babu is absolutely false and concocted. All the co-sharer of the R.S. and S.A. recorded tenants were not made parties in the suit. The Government acquired .42 acre and the rest .22 acre was duly recorded in the S.A. recorded tenants. There is a Government drain in northern side of the suit plot and thereafter Government Road; the land of the plaintiff stands distance place from the suit land. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 purchased the suit land within the knowledge of the plaintiff and others and the next day of purchase defendants took possession within the knowledge of all and constructed house. Thereafter defendant Nos. 1 and 2 rented the same to the students. The value of the suit land is increasing day by day and thus the plaintiff filed this test suit without depositing the value of the deed along with compensation. The plaintiff did not observe any formalities of talab-i-mowasibat and talab-i-ishhad. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have been possessing the suit land since their purchase. Hence, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with cost.
